# typescript-eslint 8.72.1 `consistent-type-imports`, run with vue-eslint-parser 10.4.2
# (@typescript-eslint/parser 8.72.1, eslint 10.14.0) on each SFC below: every way a
# template can use an import as a value, every look-alike that is not a use, and
# whole-component cases.
# `typescript-eslint`: its reports. `vize`: the reports of `script/consistent-type-imports`
# on its defaults. The two agree on which lines are reported, except where `kept`
# gives the reason.
=== template[0]
--- sfc
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Foo } from './foo';
defineProps<{ item: Foo }>();
</script>
<template>{{ Foo }}</template>
--- typescript-eslint
--- vize
=== template[1]
--- sfc
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Foo } from './foo';
defineProps<{ item: Foo }>();
</script>
<template>{{ Foo.label }}</template>
--- typescript-eslint
--- vize

=== template[27]
--- sfc
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Foo } from './foo';
defineProps<{ item: Foo }>();
</script>
<template><div is="vue:Foo" /></template>
--- typescript-eslint
line 2: All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
--- vize
--- kept
`is="vue:Foo"` renders the setup binding `Foo` like a `<Foo>` tag. typescript-eslint does not count that use, and its fix would leave the tag unresolved at runtime.

=== template-read-beside-prop-type
--- sfc
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Bar } from "./Foo";
import { Foo } from "./Foo";

const { item } = defineProps<{ item: Foo }>();
</script>

<template>
  <p>{{ Bar.label }} {{ item.label }}</p>
</template>
--- typescript-eslint
line 3: All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
--- vize
line 3: All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
=== style-v-bind

defineProps<{ item: Foo }>();

=== style-v-bind-quoted

defineProps<{ item: Foo }>();
</script>
<template><p /></template>

--- typescript-eslint
--- vize
=== kebab-tag

--- vize

--- typescript-eslint
--- vize
=== two-blocks
--- sfc
<script lang="ts">
import { A, B, C } from './a';
export type X = A;
export const c = D;
</script>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { D, E, F } from './d';
const b = B;
type Y = E | C;
console.log(b);
</script>
<template><p>{{ F }}</p></template>
--- typescript-eslint
line 2: Imports "A" and "C" are only used as type.
line 7: Imports "E" are only used as type.
--- vize
line 2: Imports "A" and "C" are only used as types.
line 7: Import "E" is only used as a type.
=== generic
--- sfc
<script setup lang="ts" generic="T extends Base, U = typeof Fallback">
import { Base, Fallback, Other } from './types';
defineProps<{ item: T, other: U }>();
</script>
<template><p /></template>
--- typescript-eslint
line 2: Imports "Base" are only used as type.
--- vize
line 2: Imports "Base" and "Fallback" are only used as types.
=== options-api
--- sfc
<script lang="ts">
import { defineComponent } from 'vue';
import { Foo } from './foo';
import Child from './Child.vue';
export default defineComponent({
  components: { Child },
  data: () => ({ item: null as Foo | null }),
});
</script>
<template><Child>{{ Foo }}</Child></template>
--- typescript-eslint
line 3: All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
--- vize
line 3: All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
=== type-import-read-by-template
--- sfc
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { Shape } from './shape';
defineProps<{ kind: Shape }>();
</script>
<template><p :title="Shape.name" /></template>
--- typescript-eslint
--- vize
line 2: "Shape" is imported as a type, but the template reads it as a value.
--- kept
typescript-eslint leaves a type-only import used as a value to the type checker, which cannot see the template. The binding does not exist at runtime, so vize reports the read.
